1 Important Information for Tentative Rulings and Hearings:
2
1. Please review and follow the Tentative Ruling Instructions which can be found on the Court’s website
3
using the following link: https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/unified-family-court/ufc-tentative-rulings.
4
2. If you wish to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case, you must notify the other party
5
(unless there is a restraining order in place) and the Court Clerk in the Department where the hearing
6
is scheduled of your objection by 4:00 PM the Court day prior to the hearing date. Court days do not
7
include Court holidays, Saturdays, or Sundays. The Court’s Holiday Schedule can be found on the
8
Court’s website using the following link: https://sf.courts.ca.gov/general-information/holiday-
9
schedules.
10
3. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 403 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
11
please call (415) 551–3741 or send an email to Department403@sftc.org.
12
4. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 404 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
13
please call (415) 551–3744 or send an email to Department404@sftc.org.
14
5. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 416 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
15
please call (415) 551– 3756 or send an email to Department416@sftc.org.
16
6. When you contact the Court Clerk to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case, please
17
specify the paragraph(s) and / or line number(s) of the Tentative Ruling which contains the language
18
to which you object.
19
7. You may appear at your hearing either (a) in-person; (b) by video; or (c) by phone. Pursuant to SFLR
20
11.7(D)(4), if you choose to appear by video or phone, you must be continuously connected to Zoom
21
from 8:50 a.m. until 12:00 p.m. or until your hearing is concluded (or from 1:20 p.m. until 4:30 p.m.
22
or until your hearing is concluded, if your hearing is scheduled to start at 1:30 p.m.). If you fail to
23
appear in-person, by video, or phone, the Court may proceed with the hearing in your absence. The
24
Court is not required to contact you before your hearing.
25
8. If you choose to appear by video or by phone, you must comply with the Notice and Instructions for
26
Remote Appearances in San Francisco Family Court set forth below.

2 NOTICE AND INSTRUCTIONS FOR REMOTE APPEARANCES
3 You may appear at your court hearing either (1) in-person or (2) remotely by video or telephone. If
you fail to appear in-person or remotely by video or telephone, the court may proceed with the hearing
4 in your absence. The clerk will NOT contact you. Remote appearances by video or telephone can be
made utilizing the ZOOM platform, effective January 2, 2024:

o Enter your full first and last name TO IDENTIFY YOURSELF TO THE COURT.

18 A. Procedural History
19 1) Petitioner Genevieve Torio (Mother) and Respondent Edwin Vences (Father) have one minor
20 child together, Catalina (DOB 8/23/2023, age 2). Mother lives in San Francisco; Father lives in
21 Houston, Texas.
22 2) On 11/4/2025, this Court found that Mother proved instances of domestic violence as defined by
23 Family Code section 6203 and that the Family Code section 3044 presumption against sole or
24 joint physical custody to Father applied. The Court awarded Mother sole legal and sole physical
25 custody to Mother, with parenting time for Father as follows: (1) weekly Zoom video calls on
26 Mondays and Thursdays from 6:30 to 6:45pm; and (2) in-person, professionally supervised visits
27 once monthly in San Francisco, up to 3 hours per day, up to 3 days on the selected weekend. The
28 Court issued various other orders including conduct and communication orders, scheduled a
29
1 review hearing for 3/3/2026, and ordered the parties to file and serve update declarations at least
2 10 days before the review hearing.
3 3) On 2/25/2026, Mother filed an update declaration in which she details the problems that have
4 occurred since the last hearing. Mother requests that the Zoom video calls be reduced to once per
5 week, that the in-person, professionally supervised visits be reduced to one day per month, that
6 Father pay attorney fees and sanctions, that he enroll in a 52-week batterers' intervention
7 program, and that he be ordered not to record any Zoom video calls and to delete all video call
8 recordings that he has not yet deleted.
9 4) Father has not filed an update declaration as of the time of this tentative ruling. The record shows
10 that Father filed a new request for order on 2/17/2026; this request is not currently before this
11 Court.
12 B. Findings and Orders
13 1) This Court has jurisdiction to make child custody orders in this case under the Uniform Child
14 Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act. A violation of this order may subject the party in
15 violation to civil or criminal penalties, or both. The country of habitual residence of the minor
16 children is the United States.
17 2) The parties are ordered to appear in person or via Zoom video in Department 404 at 9am
18 on 3/3/2026.

14 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
15 Court makes the following findings and orders:
16 A. Procedural History
17 1) Jonathan Roach (Father) and Devene Tobie (Mother) have one minor child together, Nasir Tobie
18 (DOB 9/20/2020, age 5).
19 2) On 7/17/2024, a juvenile custody order was filed granting the parties joint legal custody of Nasir,
20 with physical custody to Father and parenting time for Mother every week from Friday to
21 Saturday, plus additional visits, including additional overnights, as agreed upon by the parties.
22 3) On 4/28/2025, Mother filed a request for joint physical custody, with parenting time every
23 weekend, from Friday to Monday.
24 4) After the matter was taken off calendar for failure to serve Father, Mother refiled her request and
25 both parties appeared at a 12/11/25 hearing. The Court ordered that beginning on 12/19/2025,
26 Mother shall have parenting time every other weekend from Friday exchange at 6pm at the
27 MacArthur BART station in Oakland until Sunday exchange at 6pm at the Embarcadero BART
28 station in San Francisco. The Court ordered that neither party shall use any form of physical
29
1 force to discipline the child. The Court set a review hearing for 3/3/26 at 9am in Department 404
2 and ordered the parties to file and serve update declarations no later than 2/20/2026.
3 5) Neither party has filed an update declaration.
4 B. Findings and Orders
5 1) This Court has jurisdiction to make child custody orders in this case under the Uniform Child
6 Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act. A violation of this order may subject the party in
7 violation to civil or criminal penalties, or both. The country of habitual residence of the minor
8 child is the United States.
9 2) As neither party has filed an update declaration, the matter is taken off calendar. If either party
10 seeks changes to the current order and the parties are unable to reach an agreement, they may file
11 a new request for order with the Court.
12 3) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.

15 TENTATIVE RULING

20 I. Father’s Request for Order filed 1/29/2026
21
22 A. Procedural History
23 1) Petitioner Nathalie Delrue-McGuire (Mother) and Respondent Garry K. McGuire, Jr. (Father)
24 have one minor child together, Madison (DOB 1/7/2013, age 13).
25 2) On 12/5/2017, the parties entered into a Stipulation and Order in which they agreed to share joint
26 legal custody of Madison and her older brother (who has since reached the age of majority). The
27 parties agreed that in the case of a disagreement regarding issues relating to legal custody, they
28 shall jointly retain a family law mediator to hear the issue in private, confidential mediation. As to
29 physical custody, the parties agreed that the children would live with Mother, with parenting time
1 for Father on the first and third weekends of the month, four weeks during summer break, and
2 holidays. The parties agreed that in the case of a disagreement regarding physical custody, they
3 shall jointly engage the services of a family law mediator to hear the issue in private mediation
4 before filing any action in Court on the disputed custody issue.
5 3) On 12/3/2024, the parties entered into a Stipulation and Order in which they agreed to continue
6 sharing joint legal custody. They agreed that in the case of a disagreement regarding issues
7 relating to legal custody, they shall jointly retain a family law mediator to hear the issue in
8 private, confidential mediation, or to request mediation through Family Court Services if they are
9 unable to afford a private mediator. As to physical custody, the parties agreed to share 50/50
10 custody. The parties agreed that in the case of a disagreement regarding physical custody, they
11 shall jointly engage the services of a family law mediator, or a Family Court Services mediator if
12 they cannot afford a private mediator, before filing an action in Court on the disputed custody
13 issue.
14 4) On 1/29/2026, Father filed an ex parte request for emergency orders for Madison to be
15 immediately re-enrolled in Del Mar Middle School in Tiburon, where Father lives. He states that
16 Mother, who moved to Redwood City in November 2005, unilaterally removed Madison from
17 Del Mar Middle School on 1/14/2026 and enrolled her in a school in Redwood City. Father states
18 that as a result of the move, Madison has missed, and will continue to miss, “critical IEP services
19 and educational continuity.”
20 5) Mother filed a response to Father’s ex parte request, stating Father knows, and has known for
21 months, that Madison has wanted to leave Del Mar Middle School. She states that Madison has
22 been living with her in Redwood City since November 2025 and does not wish to return to her
23 former school. Mother states she did not violate Court orders by moving Madison to Redwood
24 City, as the Stipulation and Order only restricts the parties from moving the children outside of
25 the Bay Area. She states the IEP was properly transferred to the new school and is ongoing. She
26 states that Father appeared to be initially cooperative in discussing Madison's move to the new
27 school but that he filed an ex parte request in violation of the Stipulation and Order that requires
28 mediation before the filing of a Court action. She asks that Madison be permitted to stay in the
29
1 Redwood City school and that the Court order a Tier II interview of her before ruling on Father's
2 request.
3 6) The Court scheduled a hearing on Father’s ex parte request on shortened time, on 3/3/2026 at
4 9am.
B. Findings and Orders
5
1) This Court has jurisdiction to make child custody orders in this case under the Uniform Child
6
Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act. A violation of this order may subject the party in
7
violation to civil or criminal penalties, or both. The country of habitual residence of the minor
8
child is the United States.
9
2) The parties are ordered to appear in person or via Zoom video in Department 404 at 9am
10
on 3/3/2026.

22 Affidavit for Contempt filed 1/27/2026.

AM on 3/3/2026.

12 REQUEST FOR ORDER RE DIVISION OF COMMUNITY PROCEEDS FROM SALE OF RENTAL
13 HOME
14 TENTATIVE RULING
15 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
16 Court makes the following findings and orders:
17 A. Procedural History
18 1) The parties in this matter are Petitioner Swati Salunke (Wife) and Respondent Vikram Salunke
19 (Husband). The parties married on 12/25/2015 and their date of separation is 11/3/2018, for a
20 marriage of 2 years and 10 months. The parties have one minor child, Shorya (DOB: 7/17/2017).
21 Both parties are currently self-represented.
22 2) On 3/17/2022, a Stipulated Judgment resolving all issues in this matter was entered. Paragraph 8
23 of the Stipulated Judgment provides in relevant part: “The parties residence located at 555 Inness
24 Ave. in San Francisco shall be sold forthwith. The parties shall equally share in all expenses
25 pending sale. The parties shall equally divide the proceeds upon sale. This Court shall retain
26 jurisdiction to enforce the sale and the terms of this agreement.”
27 3) Following the Judgment, Husband filed three Requests for Order regarding the Inness Ave.
28 property, including the instant Request for Order.
29 4) Husband’s Request for Order filed 1/8/2023
1 a. On 8/3/2023 (per the Findings and Order After Hearing filed 8/11/2023), the Court
2 adjudicated Husband’s request to immediately sell the Inness Ave. property among other
3 requests. The Court made a finding that the Judgment includes no provision for Husband
4 to receive an additional $130,00 from the proceeds of sale and denied Husband’s request
5 that he be reimbursed $130,000 from the equity of the home. The Court noted the
6 Judgment requires the immediate sale of the property, ordered the parties to meet and
7 confer to select a listing agent, and set a compliance hearing on 8/17/2013.
8 b. On 8/17/2023 (per the Findings and Order After Hearing filed 9/1/2023), the Court
9 denied Husband’s request that it reconsider its prior order denying his request to receive
10 an additional $130,000 from the equity of the property. The Court appointed Gagan
11 Sandhu to serve as listing agent for the property and ordered that the net proceeds from
12 the sale of the property be deposited into an interest-bearing savings account in the name
13 of both parties. The Court also made a finding that the Judgment is silent regarding any
14 rental income generated by the property and made a finding that any rental income
15 generated from the property would be community property to be shared equally between
16 the parties “as it is income generated from an undisputed community asset.” The Court
17 set a review hearing for 11/7/2023.
18 c. On 11/7/2023 (per the Findings and Order After Hearing filed 11/28/2023), the Court was
19 informed that Gagan Sandhu is no longer the parties’ listing agent. The Court set a future
20 date of 11/28/2023 and ordered the parties to talk to their own agent or another agent to
21 see about possible options including foreclosure.
22 d. On 12/28/2023 (per the Findings and Order After Hearing filed 2/23/2024), the Court
23 noted that no pleadings had been filed since the 11/7/2023 hearing and removed the
24 matter from calendar.
25 5) Husband’s Request for Order filed 1/2/2024
26 a. On 3/5/2024 (per the Findings and Order After Hearing filed 6/3/2024), the Court
27 adjudicated Husband’s Request for Order filed 1/2/2024 asking the Court to find that
28 Wife owes him $113,295.47 for the property (which included $130,000 for Husband’s
29 separate property contribution claim and other reimbursements owed between the parties
1 as claimed by Husband). The Court sanctioned Husband $500 under Family Code section
2 271 for reprising his claim that he is owed $130,000 for a separate property contribution
3 to the property despite two prior Court orders stating that he is not. The Court ordered the
4 parties to comply with the Judgment and reserved jurisdiction to adjudicate what each
5 party may be entitled to or obligated for with respect to any sale proceeds, surplus funds,
6 or remaining obligations associated with the property following sale or foreclosure, as
7 neither had yet occurred.
8 6) Husband’s Request for Order filed 12/17/2025
9 a. Now on for hearing is Husband’s Request for Order filed 12/17/2025. Husband states that
10 the property was foreclosed on 10/10/2025. Husband states that in Wife’s declaration
11 filed 10/22/2023, Wife reported receiving rental income of $125,175. Husband requests
12 one-half of this amount, or $62,587.50, plus interest in the amount of $5,310.91.
13 b. On 2/13/2026, Wife filed a Responsive Declaration. Wife states that the property was
14 foreclosed on 10/10/2024, “resulting in no proceeds being generated or distributed to
15 either party.” Wife states that, since the parties’ separation, Husband did not contribute to
16 any of the property’s expenses, including mortgage, property taxes, homeowner’s
17 association fees, insurance, or maintenance. Wife also states, “Although the Property was
18 rented for a limited period following separation, all rental income received was used to
19 satisfy ongoing obligations associated with the property, including but not limited to the
20 mortgage, property taxes, insurance and maintenance. As a result, no net rental income
21 exited to be divided between the parties. During the period from March 1, 2019, through
22 May 1, 2023, the property generated total rental income of $125,175. Expenses necessary
23 to carry the Property during that same period totaled $129,153. (See Exhibit C
24 delineating income and expenses). Accordingly, the Property operated at a net rental loss
25 of $3,978.63, of which Respondent’s one-half share is $1,989.32… I listed the Property
26 for sale and undertook reasonable, good-faith efforts to effect a sale… Despite these
27 efforts, the Property did not sell… In or about January 2023, I experienced an involuntary
28 job loss and significant financial hardship, which limited my ability to continue all
29 property-related expenses without contribution. Respondent did not offer any assistance.
1 The foreclosure was not the result of neglect or misconduct.” Wife also states,
2 “Respondent cites alleged rental income without conducting due diligence or seeking
3 clarification regarding the actual financial performance of the property… Respondent has
4 filed the present motion, necessitating further expenditure of judicial resources, once
5 again… I have been compelled to respond to motions premised on allegations that ignore
6 expenses, the foreclosure, and prior Court orders… These filings unnecessarily burden
7 the Court and have caused me undue hardship, requiring the expenditure of significant
8 time and resources to respond.” Wife asks the Court to:
9 i. Order Husband to reimburse her in the amount of $1,989.32, representing
10 Husband’s one-half obligation of the net rental loss.
11 ii. Award Wife $3,000 in Family Code section 271 sanctions.
12 7) According to the Proof of Service filed 2/13/2026, Wife’s Responsive Declaration was mailed to
13 Husband on 2/12/2026.
14 8) Husband did not file a Reply Declaration.
15 B. Findings and Order
16 1) Husband’s request that the Court award him $67,898.41 is denied.
17 2) The Court finds good cause to grant Wife’s request for $1,989.32, representing Husband’s one-
18 half share of the net amount in rental income less expenses for the property (which the parties
19 were ordered to share equally pending sale per Paragraph 8 of their Stipulated Judgment)
20 following entry of Judgment. Husband shall pay this amount to Wife no later than 3/31/2026 at
21 5:00 PM.
22 3) Wife’s request for $3,000 in Family Code section 271 sanctions is denied.
23 4) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.

12 OTHER REVIEW HEARING
13 TENTATIVE RULING
14 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
15 Court makes the following findings and orders:
16 A. Procedural History
17 1) The parties in this mater are Petitioner David Carlson (Father) and Respondent Ekama Carlson
18 (Mother). The parties married on 3/31/2012. While the parties disagree regarding their exact date
19 of separation, they do agree that they separated in early 2024, for a marriage of at least 11 years.
20 The parties have two minor children, Basse (DOB: 12/26/2014) and Esien (DOB: 4/23/2021).
21 Mother is represented by attorneys Lauren Cirlin and Virginia Donnell. Father is currently self-
22 represented.
23 2) At the prior 10/9/2025 hearing (per the Findings and Order After Hearing filed 10/17/2025), the
24 Court adopted its Tentative Ruling (without objections) which requires Mother to pay Father,
25 effective 11/1/2025 $1,954 per month for guideline child support and $1,894 per month for
26 temporary guideline espousal support, for a total of $3,848 per month (based on an imputation of
27 $100,000 in annual income to Father). The Court noted that the Work Search Order against father
28 remained in effect. A review hearing was set for 3/3/2026.
29
1 3) On 2/23/2026, Father filed a Declaration Regarding Work Search and Employment Status. Father
2 states that he has continued looking for work but remains unemployed. Husband states,
3 “Respondent has not paid me spousal support since she filed her TRO in June, 2025 and owes me
4 over $40,000 in support arrears… The current situation is not sustainable for me, and I
5 desperately want to be working, especially where Respondent refuses to pay support which I need
6 to survive… despite my best efforts to secure work I have been unsuccessful. I am deeply
7 discouraged and in a dire financial situation, but I continue to pursue employment and will have
8 to take anything I can find, even if it is outside my area of expertise and well below the income I
9 hoped to earn from a new position. The Court is already imputing me income of $100,000 per
10 year, which seriously reduces the support order and is unsustainable for me. Given my
11 employment and income history, imputing any higher level of income when I have been actively
12 seeking work would be detrimental to our children as I can already not afford to pay for basic
13 living expenses.”
14 4) Per the Proof of Service filed 2/23/2026, Father’s declaration was electronically served on
15 Mother’s attorney on 2/23/2026.
16 5) Mother has not filed any pleadings regarding support since the prior 10/9/2025 hearing.
17 6) The Court notes that on 2/19/2026, Judge Chan concluded a 5-day trial on Mother’s Request for
18 Domestic Violence Restraining Order filed 6/4/2025. The parties agreed to continue the trial for a
19 period of one year, which included extending the Temporary Restraining Order for one year. The
20 parties also agreed that if there were no acts violating the Temporary Restraining Order for a
21 period of one year, Mother’s Request for Domestic Violence Restraining Order would be
22 dismissed.
23 7) The Court also notes there is a long-cause hearing coming up on 3/26/2026 in Dept. 404 on
24 Mother’s Order to Show Cause and Affidavit for Contempt (filed 10/17/2025).
25 B. Findings and Order
26 1) All orders set forth in the Findings and Order After Hearing filed 10/17/2025 shall remain in full
27 force and effect. The Court will not set any future review hearings. Either party may file a new
28 Request for Order if they wish the Court to make additional orders regarding support.
29 2) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.
